guide.title: Airway & Breathing Skills
guide.lead: Open it, clear it, keep it open, then breathe for them if they can't. Most airways are managed with positioning, suction, a simple adjunct and a good two-hand bag-mask seal. Slow, gentle breaths beat fast, big ones.

steps.title: Open
steps.text: Head-tilt chin-lift; jaw thrust if spinal injury is possible (head-tilt if the jaw thrust doesn't open it).

steps.title: Suction
steps.text: Rigid (Yankauer) for the mouth. Measure, suction on the way out, no longer than 15 seconds in adults (10 seconds in children, 5 seconds in infants). Oxygen before and after.

steps.title: Look
steps.text: Remove loose dentures and visible objects; leave well-fitting dentures for a better mask seal.

sections.title: Adjuncts
rows: Corner of mouth to earlobe (or angle of jaw)
Adults: upside down, rotate 180°. Children: right way up with a tongue depressor
Lubricate; bevel toward the septum; gentle rotation if resistance
Suspected basal skull fracture (relative), severe facial trauma

steps.title: Seal
steps.text: Two people when possible: two-hand thumb-and-palm grip with a jaw lift, partner squeezes. One person: E-C clamp.

figures.alt: Two-person bag-mask: one rescuer with both hands sealing the mask (thumbs on the mask, fingers lifting the jaw), the other squeezing the bag.

steps.title: Volume
steps.text: Just enough for visible chest rise, over 1 second.

steps.title: Rate
steps.text: Adults: 1 breath every 6 seconds. Children and infants: 1 every 2–3 seconds. CPR without an advanced airway: 30:2 (adults), 15:2 (children, two rescuers).

steps.title: Too much hurts
steps.text: Fast, big breaths inflate the stomach (vomiting, aspiration), lower venous return and blood pressure, and can cause barotrauma.

sections.title: Oxygen devices
notes: Titrate to SpO₂ 94–98%; 88–92% for COPD with CO₂ retention.

sections.title: Stoma and tracheostomy
items: A laryngectomy stoma is the only airway: ventilate the stoma with a small round mask
Tracheostomy: bag directly onto the tube; if it fails, suction, change the inner tube, or replace it
Partial neck breathers: close the mouth and nose while ventilating the stoma

options: Corner of the mouth to the earlobe
Tragus to angle of jaw only
quiz.explanation: Nostril to earlobe sizes a nasal airway.

quiz.q: Unresponsive crash victim, possible neck injury, has vomited. Sequence?
options: Jaw thrust, suction, then an adjunct (avoid the nose if a skull fracture is possible)
quiz.explanation: Head-tilt only if the jaw thrust fails.

quiz.q: Bagging at 20/min with big, slow-to-release breaths causes:
options: Gastric inflation, low blood pressure and barotrauma
quiz.explanation: Aim for 1 breath every 6 seconds, visible chest rise.

quiz.q: COPD patient on 15 L/min becomes drowsy with SpO₂ 99%. Most likely?
options: CO₂ retention from too much oxygen: titrate to 88–92% and assist breathing if needed
quiz.explanation: V/Q mismatch and the Haldane effect raise CO₂.

quiz.q: Maximum suction time in an adult:
An OPA is inserted in a child:
options: Right way up with a tongue depressor

quiz.q: Adult rescue breathing rate with a pulse:
A nasal airway is relatively contraindicated in:
quiz.explanation: Gag reflex is a reason to choose an NPA over an OPA.

options: Two-person, two-hand seal with a jaw lift

quiz.q: Patient with a laryngectomy stoma stops breathing. Ventilate:
options: Through the stoma with a small mask
quiz.explanation: The stoma is the only airway.

flashcards.question: Head-tilt chin-lift vs jaw thrust
flashcards.answer: Head-tilt chin-lift: no suspected spinal injury. Jaw thrust: possible spinal injury – but open the airway with head-tilt if the jaw thrust fails.

flashcards.question: Oropharyngeal airway
flashcards.answer: Size corner of mouth to earlobe. Adult: insert upside down and rotate 180°. Child: right way up with a tongue depressor. Only with no gag reflex.

flashcards.question: Nasopharyngeal airway
flashcards.answer: Size nostril to earlobe; lubricate; bevel toward the septum. Tolerated with a gag reflex. Caution with suspected basal skull fracture.

flashcards.question: Suction rules
flashcards.answer: Measure; suction on the way out; adults 15 seconds, children 10, infants 5; oxygen before and after; watch SpO₂ and heart rate.

flashcards.question: Oxygen device FiO₂
flashcards.answer: Nasal cannula 24–44% (1–6 L/min); simple mask 35–55%; non-rebreather 60–90%; bag-mask with reservoir close to 100%.

flashcards.question: Bag-mask technique
flashcards.answer: Two-hand seal with jaw lift and a second person squeezing is best. One person: E-C clamp. Breaths over 1 second, just enough for chest rise.

flashcards.question: Ventilation rates
flashcards.answer: Adult with a pulse or an advanced airway: 1 every 6 seconds. Child or infant: 1 every 2–3 seconds.

flashcards.question: Stoma ventilation
flashcards.answer: Small round mask over the stoma; laryngectomy patients can only breathe through it. Tracheostomy: bag onto the tube; suction or replace if blocked.

critical.scenario: Nursing home: 82-year-old unresponsive, no trauma, snoring respirations, secretions in the mouth, loose dentures, no gag. RR 6, SpO₂ 84%.
critical.question: Airway sequence?

options.t: Head-tilt chin-lift, suction (15 seconds max), remove loose dentures, OPA, bag-mask with oxygen at 1 breath every 6 seconds

critical.explanation: Check glucose and look for the cause.
critical.kpi: Performs a systematic basic airway sequence

critical.scenario: 52-year-old in respiratory distress, drowsy, gag present; SpO₂ 90% on a non-rebreather; right nostril narrowed by a deviated septum.
critical.question: Adjunct and technique?

options.t: Nasal airway sized nostril to earlobe, well lubricated, into the left nostril with the bevel toward the septum; assist ventilation if needed
No adjunct ever with a gag

critical.explanation: In the left nostril, insert tip-up and rotate gently if needed.
critical.kpi: Selects and inserts an appropriate airway adjunct

critical.scenario: You're bagging an apnoeic overdose patient alone. The abdomen is swelling and SpO₂ is falling despite chest rise.
critical.question: What's going wrong?

options.t: Breaths too fast or too big: slow to 1 every 6 seconds, just enough for chest rise; get a second person for a two-hand seal; suction ready for vomit
